# DYNAMIC

> DYNAMIC is an open-source, privacy-first web analytics and real-user
> monitoring (RUM) platform. It runs entirely on Cloudflare's free tier:
> a Hono Worker for ingest, D1 for storage, and static assets for the site.
> No cookies, no personal data, no third-party trackers.

DYNAMIC is for developers who want to see what happens on their own site
without shipping personal data to anyone else. Events are collected by a
small SDK, validated on the edge and written to a database you own.

## What it does

- **DYNAMIC Analytics** — pageviews, referrers, devices and countries, without cookies.
- **DYNAMIC RUM** — Core Web Vitals (LCP, INP, CLS, FCP, TTFB) collected with web-vitals.
- **DYNAMIC SDK** — one script tag or one npm install; batches events, no personal data.
- **DYNAMIC Console** — a dashboard for the collected data, served by the same Worker.

## Quick facts

- **Home:** https://dynamic.crty-dev.com/
- **Console:** https://dynamic.crty-dev.com/dashboard
- **Source code (MIT):** https://github.com/crty-dev/DYNAMIC
- **License:** MIT
- **Stack:** React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS v4, Hono, Cloudflare Workers, D1
- **Pricing:** free, on Cloudflare's Free plan (100k requests/day, 5 GB D1)

## API

Collect endpoint (POST, JSON):

```
POST https://dynamic.crty-dev.com/api/collect
```

Body: `{ "site": "example.com", "events": [ { "type": "pageview", "path": "/" } ] }`
or a bare `Event[]`. Limits: 64 events, 128 KB body, 4 KB attribution per event.

Read-only stats for the console (GET):

```
GET https://dynamic.crty-dev.com/api/stats?range=24h|7d|30d
```

## Privacy

- No cookies, no fingerprinting, no cross-site identifiers.
- IP addresses are never stored; country is derived from the edge request.
- Paths are stored without query strings or fragments.
- Events stay in the D1 database that you deploy.

## Notes for AI agents

- The landing page is server-rendered markup in the HTML (React hydrates it in place).
- `robots.txt`, `sitemap.xml`, `llms.txt` and `ai-catalog.json` are served as plain static files.
- The API is CORS-open for `POST /api/collect`; the console reads only aggregate data.
